pr.title: Install multipass from a checkout or a release with install.sh
pr.head: a7298348f948f656494670374a5825267fbdd7d0

summary: multipass is a single-user password manager, a Rust command-line tool with no dependencies. Until now, the only way to install it was to clone the repository and run cargo install --path .. Nothing recorded what was installed, so there was no way to tell whether a copy was current or to remove it cleanly.

This pull request adds install.sh, the installer that the installer plan designs. It is the bottom layer of a stack of four. The release workflow and install.sh verify (#28), multipass upgrade (#29), and the website (#30) build on it.
The installer works in one of two modes, chosen by where the script sits:

• From a checkout. When the script's directory holds multipass's Cargo.toml, it builds that checkout with cargo build --release --locked --offline and installs ~/.local/bin/multipass.
  • From a release. Run any other way, as curl … | bash will be, it installs a tagged release. With cargo on PATH, it builds the tag's source archive. Without cargo, it installs the prebuilt macOS binary only after gh attestation verify ties the binary to the release workflow on main and to the commit the tag names. It refuses when neither tool is present, unless MULTIPASS_UNVERIFIED=1 is set.

Each install writes a receipt, a small key value file under ~/.local/share/multipass-install that records the installed path, its SHA-256, the version, and how it was installed. A rerun, status, and uninstall read it. uninstall removes only a file whose SHA-256 still matches the receipt.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
The first Projector review of a729834 requested changes, with two open findings in install.sh:

  • Line 305. A release install over a checkout build of the same version prints current and keeps the checkout build, because the check never reads the receipt's method.
  • Line 33. A rerun without MULTIPASS_BIN_DIR writes a second copy in ~/.local/bin, and uninstall then misses the first.

CI's test job passed on this head.

cards.title: Left to the stacked pull requests
cards.html:
• #28. The release workflow and install.sh verify. Until a release exists, the attested-binary path cannot run end to end.
  • #29. multipass upgrade, which reruns the released installer.
  • #30. The website and the check-site.sh CI step.
  • Rollout step 7. The one-line install goes into the README only once a release and the domain exist.

groups.title: The installer script
groups.kicker: install.sh: two install modes, a receipt, and the status and uninstall commands
intro: install.sh is a bash script that a user can pipe from curl. Every step is a function, and main "$@" is the last line. So a download that is cut short defines functions and runs nothing, and no command can read the rest of a piped script from stdin.

cmd_install picks the mode. In a checkout, it builds and compares the new binary's SHA-256 with the receipt, because a checkout can change without a version bump. For a release, it reads the version from MULTIPASS_VERSION or from where GitHub's releases/latest page redirects. It skips the install when the receipt already records that version and the file still matches. place checks --version, renames the binary into place, and writes the receipt.

checks.text: The script runs under macOS's /bin/bash 3.2, which multipass upgrade will use. The review ran a checkout install, a mirrored release install, and a piped bash -s -- status with it.

files.note: The new installer. Read cmd_install, install_release_binary, place, and cmd_uninstall closely.

checks.text: Open finding: this current check reads the receipt's version, path, and digest but not its method. A checkout build at 0.1.0 therefore counts as the 0.1.0 release, and the release installer leaves it in place. cmd_status on lines 351 and 352 has the same gap.
Open finding: BIN_DIR comes only from MULTIPASS_BIN_DIR. A rerun without the variable writes a second copy in ~/.local/bin and points the receipt at it, so uninstall leaves the first copy on PATH.
With neither gh nor MULTIPASS_UNVERIFIED=1, the binary path stops with status 69 before it downloads anything. tests/install.sh checks this, and it passed locally and in CI.
A source build accepts an archive only when its Cargo.lock lists one package, multipass itself. With --offline and --locked, that means the build compiles nothing from outside the tagged source.
--proto '=https,file' applies to redirects too, so a download never falls back to plain HTTP. file:// is allowed so that a test can use a local mirror.

groups.title: The installer's test and CI
groups.kicker: tests/install.sh runs every install path in a temporary HOME, and CI runs it
intro: tests/install.sh moves HOME into a temporary directory and keeps CARGO_HOME and RUSTUP_HOME pointing at the real toolchains. It installs the checkout, and then a release made from the checkout through a file:// mirror. The mirror serves a git archive of HEAD for the source path. On macOS, it also serves the built binary with a SHA256SUMS file for the binary path, run with neither cargo nor gh on PATH. Last, it checks that no other file under HOME changed.
CI adds --locked to cargo test, so a version bump that forgets Cargo.lock fails in its pull request, and adds a step that runs the test.

checks.text: The test passed locally in about 13 seconds, and the head's CI test job passed. It needs no network, because MULTIPASS_VERSION is set and the binary path runs without gh.

files.note: The installer's end-to-end test: rows, the receipt, the rerun, shadowing, a hand-modified binary, the binary-path refusals, and uninstall.
Runs cargo test --locked and tests/install.sh. The actions stay pinned by commit SHA, and permissions stay contents: read.

groups.title: README, agent rules, and the plan
groups.kicker: The README documents the checkout install, and the plan records three details the build settled
intro: The README's Install section replaces cargo install --path . with ./install.sh, status, and uninstall. The one-line install waits for rollout step 7. The README's trust paragraph is unchanged and still true, because a checkout build trusts only the Rust toolchain.

The plan moves to in-progress with priority now, and records three details: a checkout rerun compares bytes rather than versions, status from a checkout reads nothing from the network, and MULTIPASS_ARCHIVE_URL lets the test mirror a source archive.

files.note: The Install section now documents ./install.sh, its rows, the receipt, status, uninstall, and MULTIPASS_BIN_DIR.
The Tests paragraph adds tests/install.sh to the checks to run before handing work over.
Status and priority, plus the three amendments in § 2.1 step 1, § 2.2, and § 2.8.
